title: Women's Asia Cup 2026 Begins August 28 With India-Pakistan Clash on September 5
excerpt: Seven-time champions India face defending titleholders Sri Lanka and arch-rivals Pakistan in the T20 tournament across 15 matches in Dubai.
body:
• The 2026 Women's T20 Asia Cup runs from August 28 to September 13 in Dubai, featuring eight teams in 15 matches under the Asian Cricket Council.
  • India, seven-time champions, will face Pakistan on September 5 in the marquee group-stage encounter at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium.
  • Sri Lanka are the defending champions after dethroning India in the 2024 final, making India's bid for an eighth title a redemption campaign.
  • Group A features India, Pakistan, Thailand, Hong Kong, and China, while Group B includes Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, UAE, and Indonesia.

The 2026 Women's T20 Asia Cup will begin on August 28 in the United Arab Emirates, with India eyeing an eighth continental title and a chance to avenge their 2024 final defeat to Sri Lanka, the Asian Cricket Council announced. All 15 matches will be played under lights at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium.

India vs Pakistan Headlines the Schedule

India and Pakistan have been drawn in the same group, with their marquee clash scheduled for September 5. The match is expected to be the tournament's most-watched fixture, continuing one of cricket's fiercest rivalries in the women's game.

Thailand face Hong Kong in the opening match on August 28. The eight teams have been split into two groups: Group A features India, Pakistan, Thailand, Hong Kong, and China, while Group B comprises Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, the UAE, and Indonesia. The top two teams from each group will qualify for the semi-finals, with the final set for September 13.

India's Redemption Campaign

India enter the tournament as the most successful team in Women's Asia Cup history, having won seven of the nine editions played since the inaugural tournament in 2004. They have claimed four titles in the ODI format (2004, 2005-06, 2006, 2008) and three in the T20 format (2012, 2016, 2022).

But the 2024 edition in Dambulla was a rare stumble. Sri Lanka defeated India in the final by eight wickets to claim their maiden title, snapping India's dominance and adding extra motivation for this year's campaign.

The squad is expected to be led by captain Harmanpreet Kaur, with vice-captain Smriti Mandhana anchoring the batting. Key players including Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Deepti Sharma, and wicketkeeper Richa Ghosh formed the core of India's recent Asian Games gold medal-winning side and are likely to feature.

"India-Pakistan clash headlines Women's Asia Cup 2026 schedule."

— Asian Cricket Council announcement

Sri Lanka's Title Defence

Defending champions Sri Lanka will look to prove their 2024 triumph was no fluke. Placed in Group B alongside Bangladesh, the UAE, and Indonesia, Sri Lanka face a relatively manageable path to the knockouts. Bangladesh, runners-up at the 2018 edition when they shocked India to win their maiden title, remain the strongest threat in that half of the draw.

Growing the Women's Game in Asia

The tournament's expansion to eight teams — with China and Indonesia joining traditional Asian cricket nations — reflects the ACC's push to broaden the women's game across the continent. The T20 format, adopted for the Women's Asia Cup since 2012, has helped attract new audiences and development nations to the sport.

The tournament also serves as an important preparation window ahead of the next ICC Women's T20 World Cup. For India, the Asia Cup offers a chance to rebuild confidence after their elimination from the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup in England, where Australia knocked them out despite Harmanpreet Kaur's explosive 56 off 27 balls in their final group match at Lord's.

With all matches under lights in Dubai's late-summer heat, conditions will test endurance as much as skill. For India, the mission is straightforward: reclaim a title they have owned for the better part of two decades.
